// p3nettail is F4's measurement of a server's tail (Burroughs #1239): Go's net on the fork's
// GOOS=wasip3 listens on the port its argv names, serves one connection from a peer outside the
// instance, writes 256 KiB to it, closes it and exits. The peer counts what reached it. Every Write
// here returns once the host has taken the bytes, so what the peer counts is what the host did with
// them after the guest closed and exited. It prints what it wrote, never the port.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"os"
)

const tailBytes = 256 << 10

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) != 2 {
		fmt.Println("usage: p3nettail <port>")
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:"+os.Args[1])
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("listen:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	c, err := ln.Accept()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("accept:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	payload := make([]byte, tailBytes)
	for i := range payload {
		payload[i] = byte(i*7 + i>>8)
	}
	n, werr := c.Write(payload)
	cerr := c.Close()
	ln.Close()
	fmt.Println("wrote", n, "bytes, write and close ok:", werr == nil && cerr == nil)
}
